purpose: Establish whether D2 has enough admissible historical TypeScript cases to fill stratum 3 of the pre-freeze cost-floor probe (primary + reserve). Selection work, performed before the manifest and therefore outside the probe's 12-hour budget.

search_frame.slot_spent_when: history inspection begins (partial clone / commit search / pickaxe) — a fast rejection spends a slot too
search_frame.early_stop_condition: one admissible primary AND one admissible reserve

admissibility_filter: a real migration PR or commit exists
the pin is its parent / base
the occurrence is in .ts/.tsx, or proven to be in the pinned TypeScript program (allowJs/checkJs)
the old value is connected to a control-flow budget
the migration witness shows the value carried over or dropped
the pinned state reproduces well enough to adjudicate
not_accepted_as_an_occurrence: a local retry loop that is not AWS client configuration
maxRetries in tests, documentation, or dead code
retry configuration authored natively under v3
a .js file merely sitting next to TypeScript
a generic wrapper option without proven delivery to a v2 client
a migration commit that changes the SDK but does not let the value's fate be traced

pre_frame_leads.rejection_reason: The maxAttempts match is a local constant DELETE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 used in a manual retry loop and in structured logging. None of the seven constructed AWS clients passes maxAttempts, maxRetries, or retryStrategy. No aws-sdk v2 anywhere, so there is no migration to localize.

pre_frame_leads.rejection_reason: The configuration is real but was authored natively under v3 — value 8 with adaptive retry mode, not a carried-over v2 number. No migration residue.

outcome.bounded_conclusion: Within the predeclared five-repository search frame, D2 yielded fewer than two admissible historical TypeScript cases and therefore has insufficient historical supply for inclusion in this probe.
outcome.scope_effect: Stratum 3 cannot be filled with D2. The manifest cannot reach eight case IDs on the current delta set.

hypothesis.statement: The observed scarcity is NOT primarily a language boundary. Three of the five framed candidates carried aws-sdk v2 inside genuine TypeScript programs; what was absent in every one of them was any configured retry count. Consumers accept the SDK's default retry behaviour, so the fact D2 describes has no occurrence to localize.
hypothesis.supersedes: The earlier guess that retry-configured v2 consumers are concentrated in JavaScript infrastructure code. The framed data partially refutes it: the v2 x TypeScript intersection is common; the v2 x TypeScript x configured-retry-count intersection is what is rare.
hypothesis.generalization_candidate: Contract facts differ enormously in occurrence density. D1's fact — an omitted optional field on subscription-creating calls — occurs at every such call site, and four of four D1 candidates carried it. D2's fact — an explicitly configured retry count — is rare by construction, because the default is the common case. A claim cell built on a low-density fact may never reach N_publish at any budget, which makes occurrence density a selection criterion for claim cells, not merely an outcome. This belongs to the taxonomy work of AMA-0.5 step 1, not to any delta.
hypothesis.status: hypothesis, generated by a five-repository frame; not established
